key_insight: CatDiT is a diffusion-transformer inverse design framework that generates novel heterogeneous catalysts while jointly controlling adsorbate type, binding energy, and catalyst class.
engineering_relevance: It offers a scalable way to accelerate catalyst discovery by narrowing huge design spaces to candidate sets that satisfy target activity and structural constraints.
method: Learns compressed latent representations of catalyst structures for efficient training and fast sampling.
Uses a generative diffusion transformer to produce valid catalysts across intermetallic alloys and oxide surfaces.
Supports multi-conditional generation with both discrete and continuous property control.
evidence_signal: For nitrogen reduction reaction design, the model produced 28 DFT-relaxed alloy candidates within the target activity window and above the pure-metal *N-*H scaling line, about a 1.5× enrichment over the source distribution.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the latent training data, and DFT validation is still required to confirm candidate viability.
paper_title: Catalyst Diffusion Transformer: Generative Inverse Design of Heterogeneous Catalysts
